purpose: Tamsulosin is mainly used to help men who have trouble urinating because of an enlarged prostate gland, a condition called benign prostatic hyperplasia or BPH. It helps relax the muscles in the prostate and bladder neck so that urine can flow more easily. It can also sometimes be used to help pass kidney stones.
how_it_works: Your prostate and the muscles around your bladder have special receptors called alpha-1 receptors that can cause them to tighten up. Tamsulosin blocks these receptors, which causes those muscles to relax. When the muscles relax, it becomes much easier for urine to flow out, so you feel less urgency, less straining, and you can empty your bladder more fully.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include dizziness, especially when you stand up quickly, a stuffy or runny nose, headache, and decreased amount of semen released during sex. Some men may also feel a little tired or have back pain.
warnings: Be careful when standing up from a sitting or lying position, as this medicine can cause a sudden drop in blood pressure that makes you feel faint or dizzy — especially when you first start taking it or after a dose increase. Tell your eye doctor you take this medicine before any eye surgery, because it can affect eye surgery outcomes. Avoid taking it with other alpha-blockers or certain blood pressure medicines without talking to your doctor first.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one 0.4 mg capsule taken once a day, about 30 minutes after the same meal each day. Your doctor may increase your dose to 0.8 mg if needed. Swallow the capsule whole — do not crush or chew it.
